metadata.title: School Accountability, Autonomy, Choice, and the Level of Student Achievement (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2003 student-level data with a two-stage sampling design (schools sampled first, then students within schools). Estimation is performed with least-squares regressions weighted by students’ sampling probabilities, and standard errors are adjusted for the hierarchical structure by using clustering-robust methods (clustering at the country level for country-level institutional variables and at the school level for school-level institutional variables). For the non-cognitive outcomes, the authors again compute student weights so that each country contributes equally, and they include country fixed effects. The report also constructs a complete analytic dataset via conditional mean imputation and includes imputation dummies and interactions to reduce bias from missing questionnaire data; thus, weighting and imputation are integrated into the estimation rather than treated as separate preprocessing steps.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Two analytic datasets are constructed from PISA 2003. The OECD-only dataset contains 219,794 students in 29 OECD countries; France is excluded because no school-level background information is available for any sampled schools. The extended dataset includes OECD and non-OECD countries (265,878 students in 37 countries); Liechtenstein, Macao, and Serbia/Montenegro are discarded due to missing internationally comparable country-level variables. For non-cognitive outcomes, observations with missing values on the Morale and Commitment, Non-disruptive Behaviour, and Disciplinary Climate indices are dropped (5.6%, 6.0%, and 0.6% respectively), and tardiness missing responses are dropped (2.2%). For cognitive outcomes, missing questionnaire data are handled via conditional mean imputation with imputation dummies and interactions included in the regressions.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report uses PISA 2003 microdata to study how school accountability, autonomy, and choice are associated with student outcomes across countries. The cognitive outcome is PISA 2003 mathematics achievement (with science and reading analyzed in the basic model), estimated using cross-country student-level multiple regressions that include a large set of student, family, school-resource, and country controls. The institutional variables—external exit exams, assessment uses (retention/promotion, grouping, school comparisons), teacher monitoring, school autonomy in budgeting/staffing/salaries/course content, and choice/competition indicators (private operation, government funding, and proxies for public-school choice)—are measured primarily from PISA school background questionnaires and supplemented with country-level data. The report applies sampling-probability weights, uses clustering-robust standard errors to reflect the hierarchical sampling structure, and imputes missing questionnaire data with conditional mean imputation while including imputation indicators. Results show sizable positive associations with cognitive achievement (e.g., external exit exams and private operation) and also improvements in several non-cognitive outcomes, with no evidence of a tradeoff between cognitive and non-cognitive skills.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD technical report using micro-econometric regression models rather than machine-learning predictive modeling. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms to extract and no ML-style target-variable performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) to populate in main_findings. The report is still empirical and provides effect estimates and robustness checks, but the schema’s main_findings table is reserved for ML predictive pipelines; therefore it is left empty by design.
